close_reason: Partial: deleted 2 dead allows in commit 6188b28. The remaining 15 are load-bearing (clippy fires on them today, contrary to bead's verification claim). Workspace-canonical fix filed as bd:JMAP-s9xo.
description:
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs carries 10 #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] annotations (lines 308, 339, 1154, 1388, 1495, 1797, 1961, 2049, 2274, 2324). The canonical jmap-mail-server carries zero such annotations.

Verification that the lint does not fire:
  cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server --all-features                                # 0 result_large_err warnings
  cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic        # 0 result_large_err warnings
  cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server --all-features --tests -- -W clippy::result_large_err  # 0 warnings

The lint is silent under default, pedantic, and explicit -W flags. The 10 #[allow] attributes therefore suppress nothing — they are dead annotations.

Engineering basis: gratuitous #[allow] attributes are noise that masks engineering intent. A future maintainer reading 'this fn explicitly allows result_large_err' will assume the lint fires here and the suppression is load-bearing, then waste cycles confirming it. Code review of any future change near these sites will repeat the same waste.

The shape of SetError (8 typed Option fields + extras Map) is non-trivial in size, but neither chat-server nor mail-server hits the 128-byte default lint threshold for BackendSetError<E>. If a future SetError field push makes the type cross the threshold, the right fix is workspace-wide (Box the SetError variant of BackendSetError, or shrink SetError itself) — not pre-emptive per-fn allows.

Fix: delete all 10 #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] lines. If a future build catches the lint firing, file a new bead at that time with the actual measured size and the workspace-canonical Box decision.

Canonical-template implication: mail-server's clean state is the propagation direction. Chat-server diverges from canonical; this finding closes that divergence.
title: 10 dead #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] annotations in memory.rs suppress a non-firing lint
